newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-Atlantic spot power firms amid gas rally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-Atlantic spot power firms amid gas rally.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in U.S. Mid-Atlantic firmed Tuesday amid the ongoing rally in natural gas prices and forecast of cold weather returning to the region later this week.
Daily generation cost steadily increased in recent days in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) district following the climb in natgas prices.
Swing gas prices delivered to utility receipt points in Philadelphia area today rose to $3.45-$3.55 per million British thermal units.
Very early discussion for December natural gas delivered to the Philadelphia city gate ranged between $3.50-$3.70.
Milder weather so far this week and comparatively cheaper residual fuel oil prices mitigated effects of the sharp jump in natural gas prices, market sources said.
"For dual-fuel units, it's cheaper to burn oil," a PJM trader said.

A Pennsylvania utility executive noted that the price differential between natural gas and one-percent sulphur fuel oil has started to narrow because rising gas prices have been pulling fuel oil values higher as well.
Expected return of the 850 megawatt (MW) Calvert Cliffs 2 nuclear power unit later today would likely keep PJM prices, especially for next-day delivery, in check.
The Lusby, Md. generating unit tripped off line last weekend due to a problem in a feedwater regulating valve.
Firm, peak electricity scheduled for Wednesday was quoted at $23.50-$24.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), compared with Monday's range of $23.25-$24.00 for Friday delivery.
Firm, off-peak PJM power for Tuesday was notationally assessed at $17.50-$18.00, against Monday's $17.00-$17.75.
December PJM deliveries were pegged at $28.90-$29.05, up from Monday's $28.45-$28.70.
January/February 1997 PJM electricity was assessed at $32.25-$32.75, a wider range than Monday's $32.40-$32.60.
July/August 1997 PJM power was quoted at $31.80-$32.10, higher than Monday's $31.65-$32.00.
Third-quarter 1997 PJM deliveries were discussed at $28.90-$29.10, up from a quote of $28.75-$29.00 on Monday.
